prompt: What is the purpose of the following lines in /etc/named.conf: zone "1.168.192.in-addr.arpa" { type master; file "named.192.168.1"; };?
choices: It tells the DNS server to forward all queries to named.192.168.1.
It tells the DNS server to use the named.192.168.1 file to search for hostnames when given IP addresses.
It defines a caching-only zone for the 192.168.1.0 network.
It tells the DNS server to transfer the 192.168.1 zone to a slave.
explanation: This block defines a reverse master zone; named uses the named.192.168.1 file to resolve IP addresses in 192.168.1.0/24 back to hostnames.
